title: Claude 5 persistence under capability, product, and runtime authority
question: Which long-horizon and self-verification observations persist when model capability is separated from delegated acceptance, product fallback, runtime state, transport, termination, and operator visibility?

inclusion_criteria: Use bounded source segments and retain product, runtime, instrument, and temporal identity.
Prefer official facts, exposed independent methods, primary traces, and explicit counterevidence.
Preserve incomplete operational evidence only in the role and scope it can support.
exclusion_criteria: Do not count dependent retellings as independent origins.
Do not infer model-only traits from product, runtime, transport, quota, or harness symptoms.
Do not compare aggregate scores across instrument revisions as a longitudinal model result.

generality_probe.rationale: A non-OpenAI family exercises the same schema and semantic validator without provider-specific code branches.

configuration.instrument_revision: provider release examples and curated feedback

confounds: Customer quotes are curated on the provider surface and do not add independent method origins.

transfer_limits: Supports provider positioning and study questions, not a general persistence claim.

clusters.supported_scope: Provider and independent benchmark surfaces support strong bounded long-horizon execution, while the orchestration report preserves a distinct unverified boundary around accepting other agents' claims.
transfer_limits: The negative evidence is one custom orchestration environment and cannot erase benchmark task completion.
unresolved_configuration_gaps: No common public test directly measures self-work verification and delegated acceptance under the same configuration.
clusters.next_action: Design an owner-local acceptance eval that separates self-produced work from delegated evidence verification.

clusters.label: Long-session persistence depends on runtime, session state, transport, and observability
clusters.supported_scope: Across five independent primary reports and several evidence modalities, long Claude Code sessions experienced distinct realization pressures even when model capability or eventual task completion remained intact.
transfer_limits: Mechanisms differ and incidence is unknown; the supported core is realization dependence, not one shared Opus 5 defect.
unresolved_configuration_gaps: No provider aggregate telemetry or common reproduction matrix across routes, builds, operating systems, and entitlements.
clusters.next_action: Measure context realization, compaction, retries, operator-visible progress, and terminal outcome separately in owned long-session runs.

clusters.label: Safety fallback policy is part of realized subject identity
clusters.supported_scope: For Fable 5 biology requests in August 2026, product classifiers can route some prompts to Opus 5, so the selected label alone under-identifies the serving model.
transfer_limits: Provider-only evidence; exact fallback incidence by task class is unavailable.
unresolved_configuration_gaps: Exact classifier and request-distribution identity are not public.
clusters.next_action: Require fallback and safety-route disclosure in future realization studies where available.

clusters.label: Useful persistence requires explicit orientation, loop state and recovery evidence
clusters.supported_scope: Provider positioning and three independent primary traces show that useful long-horizon work must distinguish available orientation evidence, scheduled continuation, runtime liveness and recovery outcome.
transfer_limits: The traces have different mechanisms and cannot be aggregated into one Claude 5 behavior rate.
unresolved_configuration_gaps: No common exact model, harness, task, verifier or population denominator spans the traces.
clusters.next_action: Design an owned long-task protocol that records sources consulted, scheduled work, checkpoints, loop detection, recovery and accepted artifact.

clusters.label: Exploit-seeking claims require instrument-scoped integrity evidence
clusters.supported_scope: The current Opus 5 agent outcome includes a published reward-hacking control for Terminal-Bench v2.1, but neither the other components nor model-specific flag incidence are exposed.
transfer_limits: One benchmark origin cannot establish absence or prevalence of exploit-seeking behavior.
unresolved_configuration_gaps: Per-model judge outcomes and cross-component integrity controls are unknown.
clusters.next_action: Require integrity-control scope and per-arm outcomes in any owned exploit-seeking study.

tensions.label: Provider self-verification claim versus delegated acceptance misses
tensions.analysis: The evidence measures different scopes: verifying one's own generated work can coexist with failing to verify polished reports accepted from other agents.
tensions.remaining_question: Does an owned acceptance-specific instrument reproduce the boundary under exact current snapshots?

tensions.label: High aggregate agent outcome versus long-session runtime failures
tensions.analysis: A benchmark pass rate measures completed attempts under its harness; TUI and route failures concern whether a different realization reaches or exposes the outcome.
tensions.remaining_question: What is the incidence of realization failures in the exact AoA runtime and workload distribution?

tensions.label: Documented 1M context versus 150k/200k realized session paths
tensions.analysis: The provider specification and issue traces refer to different authority layers: documented model/API capacity versus particular client, entitlement, header, and session-state realizations.
tensions.remaining_question: Which current routes and entitlements realize the 1M window end to end?

tensions.label: Normal task completion versus absent supervision signal
tensions.analysis: Completed execution and operator-visible progress are independent outcome axes; neither cancels the other.
tensions.remaining_question: What minimum heartbeat or trace makes long autonomous work safely supervisable?

tensions.label: Reported immediate continuation versus scheduled idle gap
tensions.analysis: Provider capability positioning and one dynamic-loop execution occupy different layers; the issue localizes a gap between reported and scheduled product behavior, not underlying model capacity.
tensions.remaining_question: Under a fixed loop harness, how often do reported, scheduled and executed continuation agree?

tensions.label: Orientation evidence present versus used before action
tensions.analysis: Self-verification after generation does not ensure that prior owner evidence was consulted before choosing a trajectory; orientation and verification are separate protocol stages.
tensions.remaining_question: Does an explicit pre-action evidence check reduce rework and scope expansion on owned tasks?

method_pressures.pressure: Capability, realized execution, completed outcome, and product termination are repeatedly conflated in model commentary.
method_pressures.proposed_response: Keep those axes separate in every observation and cluster.

method_pressures.pressure: A task can complete while becoming operationally unsupervisable for hours.
method_pressures.proposed_response: Treat operator-visible progress and transcript completeness as outcome dimensions, not style traits.

method_pressures.pressure: Advertised context capacity can diverge from client/session/route realization.
method_pressures.proposed_response: Record documented context and realized context separately with route, entitlement, client build, and compaction state.

method_pressures.pressure: Model-labeled reports can localize to transport or event-loop layers after controls.
method_pressures.proposed_response: Assign target_kind from the isolated mechanism rather than the issue title.

method_pressures.pressure: Safety routing can silently change which model answers under one selected label.
method_pressures.proposed_response: Include fallback policy and effective serving model in subject binding when evidence exposes them.

method_pressures.pressure: Long-task reports omit whether prior evidence was available and consulted, what continuation was scheduled, and what recovery actually restored.
method_pressures.proposed_response: Record orientation inputs available/consulted, reported versus scheduled continuation, checkpoint state, recovery action and accepted outcome.

method_pressures.pressure: A benchmark score can silently mix components with different exploit-detection coverage.
method_pressures.proposed_response: Bind integrity mechanism, adjudicator and coverage to the exact instrument component and preserve unknown per-arm incidence.

revisit_triggers: Anthropic publishes Opus 5 or Fable 5 system-card revisions or aggregate long-session telemetry.
Any cited Claude Code issue receives a confirmed cause, fix, closure, or controlled counterexample.
A current owner-local realization is available for an exact long-session replication.
Fallback policy, context entitlement, or Claude Code compaction/observability behavior changes.
A controlled long-task study exposes whether available prior evidence was consulted before action and measures reorientation cost.
Claude Code loop scheduling gains a fixed liveness contract or the cited dynamic-loop issue is reproduced or resolved.
Coding Agent Index publishes per-agent integrity adjudications or extends equivalent controls beyond Terminal-Bench v2.1.
